title: Cost-pulse rollback automator: micro-snapshots and KV-quarantine for safe config applies
creator: Aisha Raman
description: We need an automated rollback subsystem that reacts to sudden or sustained cost regressions while applying config changes that affect batching, caching, and routing. This ticket implements a 'cost-pulse' detector that monitors token-unit cost, per-route latency, and error-rate during staged config rollouts. Key innovations: (1) micro-snapshots: lightweight state diffs taken per shard before apply to allow targeted rewinds, (2) KV-quarantine: a prefix-based quarantine for KV/prefix cache changes so cached prefixes that cause regressions can be isolated and replayed, (3) staged micro-rollback: ability to roll back at shard/route granularity instead of full cluster revert, and (4) integration with batching/caching recommendation engine to suggest safe config deltas and simulated dry-run before apply. The goal is to reduce customer-visible regressions and cost spikes during config rollouts while preserving the ability to do surgical, low-blast-radius rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Automated rollback trigger fires when 15%+ sustained token-cost increase or 10% latency P95 regression is observed over a 5-minute canary window
System captures and stores micro-snapshots (diff + metadata) for each shard involved in the apply, and can replay snapshot to recreate pre-apply state deterministically
KV-quarantine can be applied to a set of prefixes and prevents them from serving cached entries while keeping other cache traffic unaffected
Staged micro-rollback can rollback a single shard or route within 60s of trigger and report root-cause prefix/key where available
Dry-run simulator produces cost/latency delta estimates for a given config change with confidence bands and is available in the Console prior to apply
End-to-end smoke tests and chaos scenarios included in CI; metrics dashboard and alerting for rollback events exist
Runbook updated and manual-override controls (snooze, approve, forced-rollback) present in Console
implementation_notes: Architecture: extend config-orchestrator with a pre-apply phase that creates per-shard micro-snapshots stored in S3 (diff gzipped) and records KV prefix touch-list
Cost-pulse detector: stream token-cost and latency metrics into a short-window aggregator (5m / 1m buckets) and evaluate alarm rules in the orchestrator; include hysteresis to avoid flapping
KV-quarantine: add a config flag to routing layer to honor quarantine lists; quarantine disables cache hits for specified prefixes and marks them for replay into cache asynchronously
Micro-rollback flow: orchestrator issues rollback job scoped to shard/route, applies snapshot diff reverse, invalidates affected caches, and recalculates placement/hotshard mappings
Dry-run: reuse the serving runtime's simulation harness to run a sampled traffic replay under the proposed config change and produce token-cost / latency distributions for top-5 routes
Telemetry: annotate all metrics with apply_id, snapshot_id, and quarantine_set so events are traceable in Console and Grafana
Security: micro-snapshots contain config diffs only (no customer payloads); ensure snapshots are encrypted with KMS and access-audited
risks: Snapshots may miss ephemeral runtime state (in-flight KV caches) — mitigated by short quiesce window and prefix touch-list
Quarantine could increase tail-latency for some routes if replay is not throttled — we will add backpressure and an adaptive prefetcher
False positives in cost-pulse could lead to noisy rollbacks; use multi-signal checks (cost + latency + errors) and require sustained window
Storage and cost of snapshots at scale — store diffs, TTL snapshots to 7d by default, and tier older snapshots to cheaper storage
